nodes.label: Frame 06701 - Late-Stage Dispersed Flock at Night (IPC-Siren, 2022-03-01 23:05:59)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still captured at 23:05 yet fully colour-exposed, implying house lights were on. Birds are markedly larger than in the February frames (advanced growth stage), individually resolvable, and spread almost uniformly across the whole floor rather than clustered. Many are settled/lying in a resting posture. The five pan feeders are only lightly attended. Litter is visibly darker and more compacted.
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates the late-cycle appearance shift: fewer, larger, more separable birds but near-total floor coverage, which inverts the detection difficulty from occlusion-by-crowding toward whole-frame saturation.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Siren Camera Viewpoint
nodes.description: The dominant camera installation in this chunk, labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' in the OSD, contributing five of the six frames and appearing in both the training img/ directory and the held-out img_test/ directory. Its view is more strongly barrel-distorted than the Gas camera and includes a curved dark boundary cable across the lower frame.
nodes.rationale: Because this single camera supplies frames on both sides of the train/test partition, split independence rests on temporal separation alone, not on viewpoint separation.

nodes.label: Dispersed Resting Distribution
nodes.description: The contrasting spatial state in which birds are spread near-uniformly over the available floor, largely settled or lying, with no strong attraction to the feeders and low local density variance.
nodes.rationale: Treated as the behavioural counterpoint to feeder aggregation: the ratio of dispersed-resting to feeder-clustered floor area over time is the quantity that makes flock distribution usable as a welfare or disturbance indicator.

nodes.label: Broiler Growth-Stage Progression Across Capture Dates
nodes.description: The systematic increase in per-bird pixel footprint as capture dates advance from 2022-02-22 through 2022-03-01: February frames show small, numerous birds while the March frame shows visibly larger, more separable birds occupying the same physical pen.
nodes.rationale: Apparent object scale is confounded with capture date rather than with camera distance, so a detector trained on early-cycle frames faces a distribution shift at test time and any fixed-size anchor or fixed-radius counting kernel will degrade across the grow-out cycle.
